facts.text: Risks are identified uncertain events; assumptions are propositions a plan currently depends on; issues have already happened; unknowns are questions a team knows it cannot yet answer.
facts.quote: Risks are identified uncertain events; assumptions are propositions the plan currently depends on; issues have already happened; unknowns are questions the team knows it cannot yet answer.

facts.text: Keep risks, assumptions, issues and unknowns separate rather than mixing them into one spreadsheet, because separation makes the management action for each clearer. This recommendation draws on assumption-based planning and conventional risk practice.
facts.quote: Keeping them apart makes the management action for each one clearer.

facts.text: Klein's pre-mortem, published in Harvard Business Review in September 2007, asks a team to imagine that its programme has failed and explain why.
facts.quote: Klein's pre-mortem (Harvard Business Review, September 2007) asks the team to imagine the programme has failed and explain why

facts.text: Klein's pre-mortem rests on Mitchell, Russo and Pennington's prospective-hindsight experiments from 1989, which showed that treating a future event as already having happened changes the explanations people generate.
facts.quote: It rests on the prospective-hindsight experiments of Mitchell, Russo and Pennington (1989), which showed that reasoning about a future event as if it had already happened changes the explanations people generate

facts.text: The one direct test of pre-mortems found was Veinott, Klein and Wiggins (2010), in which 178 students were assigned to baseline, critique, pros-and-cons, cons-only or pre-mortem conditions.
facts.quote: The one direct test found is Veinott, Klein and Wiggins (2010): 178 students were assigned to baseline, critique, pros-and-cons, cons-only or pre-mortem conditions

facts.text: In Veinott, Klein and Wiggins's 2010 student experiment, the pre-mortem condition reduced confidence in the plan more than baseline, critique, pros-and-cons or cons-only conditions.
facts.quote: 178 students were assigned to baseline, critique, pros-and-cons, cons-only or pre-mortem conditions, and the pre-mortem reduced confidence in the plan most

facts.text: The authors of the one direct pre-mortem test found, Veinott, Klein and Wiggins (2010), are linked to the method's originator.
facts.quote: the authors are linked to the method's originator

facts.text: Evidence that pre-mortems reduce failures or improve outcomes in complex engineering programmes was not found.
facts.quote: Evidence that pre-mortems reduce failures or improve outcomes in complex engineering programmes was not found

facts.text: Pre-mortems are supported only for reducing overconfidence; applying pre-mortems in management remains practitioner practice.
facts.quote: Verdict: supported for reducing overconfidence only; the management application is practitioner practice.

facts.text: For the virtual-validation programme, run one pre-mortem early and one before the delivery-readiness gate.
facts.quote: Run one pre-mortem early and one before the delivery-readiness gate

facts.text: Use a concrete pre-mortem scenario for the virtual-validation programme: it is August 2027, the safety review board has rejected the virtual-testing results, and the team must explain what happened. August 2027 is a hypothetical scenario date, not a reported rejection.
facts.quote: "It is August 2027. The virtual-testing results were rejected by the safety review board. What happened?"

facts.text: Require the virtual-validation programme's pre-mortem to identify causes across technical, evidence, schedule, supplier, people, governance and communication categories.
facts.quote: Require causes across technical, evidence, schedule, supplier, people, governance and communication categories.

facts.text: ISO 31000:2018 and IEC 31010:2019 document risk-register and risk-matrix practice.

facts.text: Maintaining a risk register is standard project-management practice.

facts.text: Outcome evidence for risk-register and risk-matrix practice is thin.

facts.text: De Bakker, Boonstra and Wortmann's 2010 meta-analysis reviewed 29 publications and found that only two papers reported some positive impact of risk management on IT project success.

facts.text: Much of the value of risk management runs through communication among stakeholders, according to De Bakker, Boonstra and Wortmann's 2010 meta-analysis.

facts.text: A useful record for each risk contains cause, possible event, consequence, owner, probability or range, impact, early warning or signpost, preventive action, trigger, contingency, and the evidence required to retire the risk.

facts.text: Colour risk matrices, including 5 by 5 heat maps, have documented mathematical flaws: Cox (2008) showed poor resolution, range compression and ranking errors.

facts.text: Work subsequent to Cox's 2008 study confirms problems with ordinal scoring in risk matrices.

facts.text: Risk registers are documented practice, whereas risk heat maps are popular but contradicted by evidence.

facts.text: Prefer quantified ranges and a ranked table for risk management; include a heat map only for familiarity, never as the basis for prioritization.
